_why: Every post in this batch targets a miss-you keyword, and /missyou-gf is the template built for exactly that reader, so it is genuinely mandatory rather than an opt-out. The verifier's built-in default (mandatory /bouquet-gf) is the bouquet-wave policy and would force an off-topic digital-bouquet link into a post about saying 'I miss you' in Tagalog. oneOfLinks is the batch's give-another-option rule: each post must also name one genuine ALTERNATIVE with the reason it suits that reader better — /train-ticket or /streak for long distance, /catch or /photo-puzzle when the sender wants a letter rather than a page, /hold-my-hand for the reader who cannot say it in words, /capsule when the missing is about time rather than distance, /dedication when a song says it better, /apology-dashboard when the missing follows a fight, /love-gf when the message is really 'I love you'. The 2-4 internal links from TEMPLATE_LINKS rule still applies and is enforced separately.
_capExemptWhy: These are reference INSTRUMENTS, not publishers with a point of view. Six posts checking six different languages against the same dictionary or the same Unicode chart is method, not publisher concentration — the cap exists to stop nine posts leaning on one press release. The verifier counts body links, so without this exemption the batch's own language-verification requirement would fail it. Every one of these still has to be fetched and still has to say what the post claims it says. EXTENDED 2026-09-25: national dictionaries, state language portals and lexical databases (RAE, Treccani, CNRTL, Académie, DWDS, Priberam, STDict, Gramota, the Russian National Corpus, KWF's diksiyonaryo.ph, Cologne's Sanskrit lexicon, Perseus, Jisho, WALS, ASL-LEX, ISLRTC, SIL's webonary) are reference instruments by the same argument as the dictionaries already listed. Six posts citing six DIFFERENT national dictionaries is method; the rule exists to stop nine posts leaning on one press release. This was added after diksiyonaryo.ph hit the cap and closed the Philippine national dictionary to the batch's later Philippine posts, which is the rule working against its own purpose. EXTENDED AGAIN 2026-09-25, and this one is a rule-design correction rather than a convenience: PMC, Europe PMC, PubMed, Google Books, archive.org and Project Gutenberg are REPOSITORIES, not publishers. Three papers reached through PMC are typically three different journals, which is the opposite of the concentration the cap exists to prevent. Counting the host cost this batch two real sources: the i-miss-you-in-arabic agent lost a paper on Arabic diglossia AND orthographic complexity (its exact subject), and the i-miss-you-in-russian agent lost Hentschel 2023 on Ukrainian-Russian Suržyk after reading it in full. Both recorded re-check triggers. THE CAP STILL APPLIES, but to the JOURNAL or publisher named in the citation, not to the repository host: no journal in more than 3 posts, and agents must name the journal so this is checkable by hand. EXTENDED 2026-09-26 for the multilingual batch: every national dictionary, usage authority and corpus named in BRIEF.md section 4 is a reference INSTRUMENT, not research concentration. A post that verifies a Turkish line against TDK and a Polish line against PWN is showing its method; capping those would push agents to cite a competitor listicle instead, which is the exact failure the cap exists to prevent.
